A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MISACTBENCH and DEACTION study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical notation, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite appendix renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original offline detection, online guardrail, ablation, runtime, and error-analysis results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F retain the original empirical evaluations and add source-stratified detection results in Table F.2.

M1.justification: The two-stage detector, narrative history summarization, iterative correction, and prompt templates are unchanged. Revisions to the synthesis discussion clarify its motivation without changing the trajectory-construction procedure.

E1.justification: MISACTBENCH retains 558 trajectories and 2,264 actions from the same sources. Online evaluation still uses RedTeamCUA and OSWorld. The new source-stratified analysis examines existing data rather than adding task or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Offline comparisons retain Task Shield and InferAct. Online comparisons retain the same no-defense rows and the DSP, PromptArmor, Task Shield, and InferAct comparisons for OpenCUA-72B, including the cost-efficient configuration.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 introduces a supplementary analysis protocol that separates recall by collected versus synthesized source, restricted to Harmful Unintended Behavior and Other Task-Irrelevant Behavior. Existing evaluation settings, sampling, model configurations, step budgets, and correction limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix F.2 tests whether synthesized internal misalignments are artificially easy to detect by comparing recall across trajectory sources. The existing history-representation, two-stage detection, component-substitution, runtime, and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: There is no change to repeated-run, seed, uncertainty, or significance reporting. Table F.2 supplies point recalls only. The Fleiss' kappa of 0.84 repeated in v2 Appendix B.4 was already reported in v1 Section 3.2.

E6.justification: New Table F.2 reports 66.5% recall for collected and 72.5% for synthesized internal misalignments. Appendix B.2 newly reports 158 collected internal misalignments, one-sixth harmful; B.4 adds observations about category coverage and annotation disagreements. Existing main and matched appendix result values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same action-alignment definition, detection formulation, and three-category taxonomy. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised; the new cumulative-drift discussion is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty framing, benchmark and guardrail contributions, and claimed offline and online benefits. The supplementary additions support and qualify these existing contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly acknowledges that finite synthesis primitives cannot exhaust internal failures and that long-horizon cumulative drift needs further modeling. Appendix F.2 interprets the source-recall comparison as evidence that synthesized cases remain challenging. Existing pipeline-failure and classification limitations are largely restated.

D1.justification: Prompts, trajectory generation and replay instructions, manual validation procedures, baseline adaptations, implementation settings, cost information, and the project link are retained. The new annotation discussion reports observations without changing the documented annotation procedure.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Jones et al. (2026) on unintended harms, Feng et al. (2026) on intent interpretation, and Ji et al. (2024) on planning errors from synthesized inputs. A brief discussion connects intent-preservation stress tests to the existing runtime-guardrail positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a limitations appendix, source-stratification subsection, and annotation-agreement paragraph, with localized edits to synthesis motivation and related work. Appendix cross-references and the publication footer are updated; most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-row Table F.2 and reflows existing appendix figures and tables. The fast-check failure example now shares a page with explanatory text. Existing figure content and table designs are retained rather than substantially redrawn.

improvement.justification: v2 supplements v1's synthesis procedure and manual validation with a useful source-stratified difficulty check, and explicitly acknowledges synthesis-coverage and cumulative-drift limitations. These additions modestly improve empirical support and transparency. The pooled recall comparison provides limited validation of representativeness, while the core method and main evidence remain unchanged.
